assessment_summary: The proof attempts to use an ear decomposition to show that if every face boundary is an even cycle, the graph is bipartite. However, in line 0029, it makes a mathematically false claim about the parity of paths in a proper 2-coloring, stating that if the length of a path P is odd, the other endpoint receives the same color as the starting point. This is backward: in any proper 2-coloring, an odd-length path always connects vertices of different colors. (The proof actually contradicts its own error by correctly stating the parity rule later in line 0036). Because this false parity logic is used to justify the validity of the ear decomposition step, the proof's logical chain is broken.
counterexample: Consider an ear P of length 1 (which is an odd length) consisting of a single edge $e = (u, v)$ being added to a properly 2-colored subgraph H. Suppose the starting endpoint $u$ is colored Red. Following the rules of alternating proper 2-coloring along P, the other endpoint $v$ must be assigned the color Blue. Since Blue is distinctly different from Red, the other endpoint $v$ does NOT receive the same color as the starting point $u$. This explicitly refutes the universally claimed implication in line 0029 that "If the length of P is odd, the other endpoint would receive the same color as the starting point".
